sources.entry: EMQX - Scalable MQTT broker. Connect 100M+ IoT devices in one single cluster, move and process real-time IoT data with 1M msg/s throughput at 1ms latency. (Demo, Source Code) Apache-2.0 Docker/Erlang

summary.one_liner: EMQX is a scalable MQTT broker and IoT data platform for connecting large numbers of devices and routing and processing their messages in real time.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes EMQX as an MQTT platform supporting MQTT 5.0, 3.1.1 and 3.1, plus MQTT over QUIC, and other IoT protocols such as LwM2M, CoAP and MQTT-SN through gateways. It advertises clustering for 100M+ concurrent clients, masterless clustering, and an SQL-based rule engine for filtering and transforming in-flight data. It lists data bridges to message queues (Kafka, RabbitMQ, Pulsar, RocketMQ), databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Redis, ClickHouse, InfluxDB) and cloud services, plus webhooks. Security features named include TLS/SSL, WSS, username/password, JWT, PSK, X.509, ACLs, and LDAP/SQL/Redis authentication. Observability is covered via Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog and OpenTelemetry, along with a dashboard and HTTP API. The README also describes a message queue feature, a drag-and-drop flow designer, and a schema registry.
use_cases: Connect and manage millions of IoT devices over MQTT
Route and filter real-time sensor or telemetry messages
Bridge IoT data into Kafka, databases or cloud services
Run a highly available MQTT broker cluster
Industrial IoT and connected vehicle data pipelines
Authenticate IoT clients with certificates, JWT or LDAP
how_to_run: Follow the Install EMQX Using Docker guide for further instructions
Build from source: git clone the repository, cd emqx, make
Kubernetes: see the official EMQX Operator documentation
notable: Supports MQTT 5.0, 3.1.1 and 3.1, plus MQTT over QUIC
Masterless clustering with clustering across sites via Cluster Linking
SQL-based rule engine with 50+ integrations listed
Built-in message queue with TTL, size limits and last-value semantics
Official Docker image and Kubernetes operator
caveats: Since v5.9.0 the license is the Business Source License 1.1, not Apache 2.0 as the awesome-selfhosted listing states; clustering more than one node requires a license file
The Docker quick start uses the emqx-enterprise image
Building requires the EMQX fork of Erlang/OTP; upstream OTP is not supported
summary.license: Business Source License (BSL) 1.1 from v5.9.0 (README); earlier versions were Apache-2.0
